summary: A May 1930 Florida Times-Union item, quoted on a Forest Lookouts page, says the Wakulla lookout tower was manned from February 2 and drew 2,127 visitors by May 20.

facts.status_note: No source found says whether the Wakulla lookout tower stands today.

events.note: Manned from February 2 of that season, per a May 27, 1930 item. It reports 2,127 visitors between then and May 20.

evidence.supports: Tower manned from February 2; 2,127 visitors between then and May 20, 1930
evidence.quote: between the time the Wakulla lookout tower was manned February 2, and May 20 there were 2,127 persons who visited the tower

evidence.supports: Item datelined Crawfordville, May 26, on a page dating it May 27, 1930
Figures credited to G. A. Young, assistant state forester, Tallahassee
evidence.quote: according to G. A. Young, assistant state forester, Tallahassee

evidence.supports: Young to visit Wakulla County to bring more property into fire protection
evidence.quote: Mr. Young will visit Wakulla county within the next few days with a view of enlisting additional property for fire protection.

evidence.supports: Department at Tallahassee pleased with the start made in the county
evidence.quote: The department at Tallahassee is extremely well pleased with the start made in this county

sources.title: Crawfordville - FOREST LOOKOUTS (quoting The Florida Times-Union, May 27, 1930)

notes_for_editor: Only one source: a catalogue page quoting a 1930 Times-Union item. The story is about 117 words, below the 120-word floor, because nothing else was found; it has no build date, design, height or fate. Searches returned the Old Wakulla County Courthouse in Crawfordville, which is not the lookout. A towerdex record for a 128.6 m tower in Crawfordville, registered to Wakulla County and dated 2009, is a different structure and no source links it to the 1930 tower. The Florida Memory newspaper pages returned 403 to fetch_text, so the primary newspaper was not checked. Record fields status and access were left as unknown; no access level is asserted.
